newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Liberals rule out joining new Russian government.
newsitem.headline: Liberals rule out joining new Russian government.

text.p: The leader of Russia's main liberal opposition party, Yabloko, on Tuesday ruled out joining the new government but offered support for reformist First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov.
"Yabloko is prepared to support any reasonable initiative by Nemtsov in parliament. We have reached agreement on this," Grigory Yavlinsky told reporters after talks with Nemtsov.
But he added: "We will not join the government and discussion of this question is over."
Nemtsov was brought into the government earlier this month after President Boris Yeltsin decided to jump-start reforms with a dramatic cabinet reshuffle.
The president then ordered Nemtsov to negotiate with Yabloko to bring in other like-minded liberals.
But Yavlinsky said on Tuesday that his party still had its doubts about the government and he called on its supporters to join a nationwide protest planned for Thursday.
"We cannot support the government because we consider that its political course is unrealistic," he said.
Nemtsov has never been a member of Yabloko, but he had close ties with the party in the Nizhny Novgorod region east of Moscow, where he was governor before joining the government.

One of two new first deputy prime ministers, Nemtsov will be in charge of dealing with Russia's powerful monopolies and with reform of the social sector -- both highly sensitive areas of the struggling and crime-ridden economy.

Yavlinsky said Nemtsov had a key role in the government and that Yabloko, which tries to promote Russia's emerging entrepreneurial class, was prepared to back him up with advice and expert help if he needed it.

"We will do all we can so that Nemtsov is not made into a decoration, so that he's not made a fool of just to extend the life of the government, because everyone understands that he was invited so as to extend its life for two or three months."
